fixes.explanation: That's their question, baker. They ask, “In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven?” and add that all of them were married to her (Matthew 22:28). They've lined up seven brothers like dominoes and want Jesus to pick one. Notice the question is built on the idea that she would be married to one of them in the resurrection.

Humble is a fine word, baker, but not what Jesus says here. He says, “He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.” (Matthew 22:32). The contrast is between the dead and the living. Put those two together and the verse sticks.

Matthew doesn't say the crowds were offended. He says, “When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.” (Matthew 22:33). Seven brothers and a tangled question, and the crowds walk away amazed. That's a whole different reaction than being offended.

Troubled isn't the word, baker. Matthew says, “When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.” (Matthew 22:33). Astonished is more like standing there with your mouth open, forgetting you were holding a cookie. The crowds were amazed at what Jesus taught.
